en: Itivuttaka 80:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Discourse on Thoughts.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One; thus have I heard:
"Monks, there are these three unwholesome thoughts."
Which three?
Thoughts associated with contempt, thoughts associated with gain, honor, and fame, and thoughts associated with concern for others.
These, monks, are the three unwholesome thoughts.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“Bound by the desire for non-contempt...”
He honors gain and honor;
he rejoices with his ministers,
yet he remains far removed from the destruction of the fetters.
But that bhikkhu who, having abandoned children and cattle,
as well as marriage and social gatherings,
is capable of such a state— such a one is worthy.
"I have touched the supreme enlightenment.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
First.
